title: Finite cohomology of a projective twist over an affine Noetherian base
statement: Let $T$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme] with Noetherian ring $A=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$, and let $N$ be a finite coordinate type. For each integer $m$ and natural number $q$, the cohomology $H^q(\mathbb P(N;T),\mathcal O(m))$ [pqf-def-cohomology] of the projective twisting module [def-pc-projective-space-twist] is a finite $A$-module, with action restricted along the projective projection [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change].

proof.text: Work directly over the affine base T, with A=Gamma(T,top). The standard intersection is the pullback of the integral-model basic open. The affine pushout of global rings and the integral Laurent-monomial basis give a bijective A-linear coefficient-to-section map. Shift the degree-zero exponents by m at any coordinate of the nonempty intersection and use its free twist generator. No choice of an affine-base isomorphism is needed.

Assemble these basis maps into a chain isomorphism between the standard-cover Cech complex restricted along the projective projection appTop and monomialCechComplex N A m. The restriction rule for twistMonomialSection and the alternating face sum prove compatibility with the differential. The separated affine-cover Cech comparison and restrictionScalarsHomologyIso give an A-linear equivalence from twist cohomology to monomial homology.

Use the ring-general algebraic formulas in WeilConjectures.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpace.MonomialCech underlying the twist-cohomology calculation, rather than its Field-only wrappers in Cohomology.Serre. For nonnegative twists degree zero is the homogeneous polynomial submodule, finite by homogeneousSubmodule_fg. For negative twists and at least two coordinates degree zero is zero. Top homology is the finitely supported functions on negativeExponents; negativeExponentsEquiv identifies that type with fixed-degree natural monomials when m<=-d-1, and otherwise it is empty. Finsupp.finite_of_degree_eq and Module.Finite.equiv prove finiteness. The single-coordinate negative-twist case uses the same top-degree formula. Middle degrees are exact by exactAt_monomialCechComplex.

Prove the general finite-affine-cover bound: for any scheme X separated over an affine T, any finite affine open cover indexed by N, and any quasi-coherent module, H^q vanishes when q>=Nat.card N. The alternating cover complex has zero degree-q term because no strictly increasing tuple of length q+1 exists in N. Alternating Cech comparison and separated affine-cover comparison transfer this to ordinary cohomology. Apply this general bound to the standard projective cover, including the empty-coordinate case. In lower degrees transport finite monomial homology along the explicitly A-linear comparison, with scalar structure exactly restriction along the projection appTop.

lean.statement:
theorem finite_H_twist_affine {T : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine T]
    [IsNoetherianRing Γ(T, ⊤)] (N : Type u) [Finite N] (m : ℤ) (q : ℕ) :
    letI : Module Γ(T, ⊤) ((twist N T m).H q) :=
      Module.compHom _ (ℙ(N; T) ↘ T).appTop.hom
    Module.Finite Γ(T, ⊤) ((twist N T m).H q)
